brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Stack of full hex bases at 0,0,0 and 0,0,1 (piece:0,0,0;full + piece:0,0,1;full) with snap joint, capped and lock-jointed; height ~160mm.
Two half-n drawer modules on south faces at 1,0,0 and 1,0,1 (drawer:0#1,0#cut lower, drawer:1#1,0#cut upper), both functional; lower opened for visibility.

Compact tower footprint (~191x171mm per base) with drawer compartments dressed (e.g., prop:2 heap-screws-div3 showing small-parts storage) – appropriate for bench organisation; no load-bearing or hazardous claims.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey tower (full bases at 0,0,0 and 0,0,1) with two south-facing half-n drawers (levels 0 and 1). Capped open faces and lock-jointed. One drawer opened to show interior compartment with workshop small-parts props; verified clear mesh and no rule errors.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
